title: Enterprise RAG Pipeline & LLM Gateway
subtitle: Semantic caching, ACL-filtered hybrid retrieval, reranking & SLM fallback
overview: Modern 2025–2026 GenAI system design blends deterministic security boundaries (RBAC/ACL enforcement, TPM rate limits, PII guardrails) with probabilistic retrieval and hardware-constrained GPU inference. A production RAG pipeline enforces permissions BEFORE retrieval, fuses BM25 + HNSW vector search, reranks top candidates, and streams tokens via SSE.
firstPrinciplesStory: You plug an LLM straight into company docs using naive vector search. On day one, two serious bugs surface: an intern asks about executive compensation and the LLM leaks restricted HR chunks filtered out *too late*; then a search for error code `ERR_9914_TIMEOUT` fails completely because pure cosine embeddings miss exact alphanumeric strings! Treating retrieval, ACLs, semantic caching, and GPU inference as a composable deterministic-plus-probabilistic pipeline (DDIA Ch. 12 unbundled derived views!) turns a fragile demo into a trustworthy system.

adaptiveLenses.intuition: Think of Enterprise RAG like an open-book exam with a strict security librarian: before the smart analyst (LLM) sees a single page, the librarian verifies your badge (ACL pre-filter), pulls exact keyword matches AND conceptual matches (BM25 + Vector), checks a sticky note of recently verified identical questions (Semantic Cache), and trims 50 pages down to the best 6 before writing a cited reply.
adaptiveLenses.mechanics: AI Gateway runs fast PII/injection guardrails and reserves dual RPM+TPM quotas in Redis. ACL-hashed semantic cache short-circuits repeats; otherwise dense HNSW + sparse BM25 retrieve with mandatory `acl IN user_groups` pre-filter, fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), pruned by a Cross-Encoder Reranker, and streamed via SSE from a continuous-batching vLLM cluster.
adaptiveLenses.staffTradeoffs: Keep probabilistic LLMs strictly outside deterministic state boundaries: never let unvalidated LLM output mutate permissions or skip ACL pre-filters. Balance TTFT (<400ms) vs recall by capping reranker candidates (top 50 -> top 6) and maintaining a quantized 8B SLM fallback for GPU KV-cache overload.

ddiaAnchors.concept: Keeping Search, Vector & Cache Indexes Synchronized via Streams
ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: Document updates and ACL permission changes must propagate reliably from source-of-truth permissions into vector & BM25 indexes via CDC/streams.

pragmaticTips.tip: Wrap inference providers behind a unified gateway contract so swapping frontier models, open-weight SLMs, or embedding versions requires zero app rewrites.
pragmaticTips.application: Route routine traffic to quantized SLMs when GPU queues spike while preserving the same SSE & citation contract.

keyTakeaways: Always push user ACL/group filters INSIDE the vector/BM25 query predicate—never post-filter after LLM generation.
Semantic caching bypasses expensive GPU prefill/decode when cosine similarity >= 0.95 for identical tenant scope.
Graceful degradation routes non-critical or overloaded traffic from frontier models to a quantized SLM when GPU KV-cache saturates.

nodes.label: Enterprise User
nodes.summary: Authenticated employee expecting cited answers with TTFT < 500ms.
failureModes: Streaming disconnect loses partial generation if unpersisted

nodes.label: AI Gateway + Guardrails
nodes.summary: Enforces Token-Per-Minute quotas, scans for prompt injections/PII, and extracts user ACL groups.
failureModes: Heavy classifier guardrails inflate TTFT if run synchronously without small fast models

nodes.label: Semantic Cache
nodes.summary: Caches `(tenant_acl_hash, query_embedding) -> cited_answer` to slash LLM cost & latency by 30–60%.
whenToUse: Repeated FAQ or team knowledge queries
failureModes: Returning cross-tenant cached answers if ACL scope isn't part of the cache key!

nodes.label: Hybrid Retriever (BM25+HNSW)
nodes.summary: Runs sparse lexical BM25 + dense HNSW vector search with mandatory `acl_group IN user_groups` pre-filter, fused via RRF.
whenToUse: Exact keyword + semantic recall across PDFs, wikis, tickets
failureModes: Strict selective ACL post-filtering collapses recall unless pre-filtered inside HNSW

nodes.label: Cross-Encoder Reranker
nodes.summary: Scores top-50 fused candidates precisely so only high-signal grounded chunks enter the LLM context window.
failureModes: Latency scales linearly if too many candidates are passed

nodes.label: LLM GPU Pool (vLLM)
nodes.summary: Executes continuous batching with KV-cache block sharing and streams grounded tokens + citations.
failureModes: VRAM OOM preemption on sudden long-context prompt spikes

steps.info: Prompt passes injection classifier; TPM bucket reserves 2,500 tokens
steps.payloadInspector: User: eng_42 | ACLs: [eng, all-staff] | TPM Remaining: 184,000
steps.inspectorNote: Deterministic auth & fast guardrail checks run before touching vector stores or expensive GPUs.

steps.info: Best cosine match = 0.84 (< 0.95 threshold) within user's ACL hash -> Miss
steps.inspectorNote: Scoping semantic cache by ACL hash guarantees confidential HR/finance answers never leak to unauthorized employees.

steps.info: Dense HNSW + Sparse BM25 fused via RRF with pre-filter `acl IN [eng, all-staff]` -> 50 chunks
steps.payloadInspector: Filter: metadata.acl ANY ['eng','all-staff'] | Fusion: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60)
steps.inspectorNote: Hybrid search captures exact error codes/acronyms (BM25) AND conceptual phrasing (Dense Vector).

predictPrompt.prompt: Why does enforcing ACL permissions inside the vector/BM25 query (`acl IN user_groups`) matter far more than filtering unauthorized results *after* retrieving top-10 matches?
predictPrompt.hint: What happens if all top-10 semantic matches belong to an executive HR folder the caller cannot read?
predictPrompt.reveal: Post-filtering leaves 0 allowed chunks (empty recall failure!) AND risks leaking confidential snippets into logs, caches, or prompt windows. Pre-filtering inside the index guarantees both security isolation and full top-K permitted recall.

steps.info: 50 candidates pruned to top 6 highest-relevance passages with doc_id citations
steps.inspectorNote: Trimming irrelevant chunks reduces TTFT, lowers inference cost, and sharply improves answer faithfulness.

steps.info: First token arrives at 280ms total TTFT; output moderation + citation tags streamed
steps.inspectorNote: Continuous batching and prefix caching on the system prompt keep TTFT well under the 500ms interactive UX budget.

chaosScenarios.title: Frontier GPU KV-Cache Saturation -> SLM Model Routing Fallback
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: H100 frontier pool hits 98% KV-cache HBM utilization during a company all-hands traffic surge.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: AI Gateway sheds heavy frontier routing for standard Q&A, downshifting to an 8B quantized SLM pool and serving semantic cache hits.

steps.payloadInspector: LoadSignal: frontier-70b saturated -> Trigger ModelRouter Fallback Policy
steps.inspectorNote: Letting queues pile up causes cascading client timeouts and wasted compute on abandoned requests.

steps.info: Routed to FP8 8B SLM fallback with top-4 chunks -> TTFT restored to 190ms
steps.inspectorNote: Grounded with top reranked chunks, a smaller SLM still gives accurate cited answers at 1/8th GPU memory.

pros: High recall on both exact IDs/terms and semantic intent
cons: Requires maintaining both inverted and HNSW indices
tradeoffs.bestFor: Production enterprise RAG over technical docs, policies, and tickets

cons: Cannot reflect real-time doc edits or per-user ACL permissions
